## PRE-FLIGHT (execute ALL in parallel before reading anything)

```bash
git log --oneline -7                        # recent history + commit style
git status --short                          # uncommitted changes
git diff HEAD --stat                        # change scope
npx tsc --noEmit 2>&1 | tail -20           # TypeScript strict check
docker ps --filter "name=mcorch" --format "{{.Names}}: {{.Status}}"
docker ps --filter "name=mega-brain" --format "{{.Names}}: {{.Status}}"
curl -s http://localhost:8001/api/v2/heartbeat  # Chroma API v2 health
ls docs/bok/ 2>/dev/null                    # BoK suites disponíveis
wc -l HANDOFF.md                            # total lines — drives the read-from-end offset
```

Read in parallel (HANDOFF.md uses **read-from-end strategy** — SSP-01 v6.5.0; monolítico newest-first, **~10k+ linhas e crescendo** — rode o `wc -l` do pre-flight, NÃO assuma um total fixo):
- `HANDOFF.md` with `limit=30` → FIRST ACTION FOR NEXT AGENT + o topo do Task State (a 1ª linha do Task State = a fase mais recém-selada; é o que importa).
- ⚠️ **TOKEN-CAP GUARD (aprendido 2026-07-19):** as linhas do Task State e dos Records são **parágrafos densos (2-4k chars cada)** — uma janela de 55-400 linhas pode **estourar o teto de 25k tokens do Read** e falhar. **Regra:** leia em janelas de **≤150 linhas**; se o Read retornar erro de token-cap, **corte a janela pela metade** e repita. Nunca insista numa janela grande "porque o doc manda".
- Para o Record mais recente (últimas 1-2 fases seladas): comece em `offset ≈ (total − 40)` com `limit=20` (pega a última linha do Task State) e depois leia o bloco `## … Record` mais novo em janelas ≤150 linhas subindo. As seções de sufixo (Pending Actions · GraphRAG State · Infrastructure · Key Files) ficam **no `CLAUDE.md`/`sprint-priorities`**, não no fim do HANDOFF.md — priorize aquelas.
- 📌 **Se `wc -l HANDOFF.md` > ~4000:** o arquivo está pesado demais p/ pickup eficiente — sinalize nos ALERTAS que o `/handoff` deveria **arquivar Records antigos** (ver Phase 5 do seal). Um HANDOFF.md enxuto (Task State + ~12 Records recentes) é o alvo.
- `CLAUDE.md` (architecture rules, data flow, key files — incluindo MCORCH Master Execution Protocol + Survival Laws link)
- `.claude/context/sprint-priorities.md` (sprint goal, 4Cs snapshot, top gaps)
- `/home/ubuntu/.claude/projects/-home-gcrUX-htdocs-constellation-orchestra/memory/MEMORY.md` (memory index)

> ⚠️ **Auditoria histórica de seals antigos:** usar `Read` com offset arbitrário em HANDOFF.md (fora do fluxo padrão de pickup). Ordering newest-first: seal mais antigo ≈ linha 2805, seal mais recente logo após linha 71. Cada `## <Phase> Record (YYYY-MM-DD)` marca um seal. Manter o Read em chunks ≤ 400 linhas para preservar budget de tokens.

Also check for loose files in scratch/:
```bash
ls scratch/ 2>/dev/null && echo "⚠️ scratch/ has files — consider moving to .claude/scripts/db/" || echo "scratch/ clean ✅"
```

### BoK Gate check (v3 — MCORCH Master Execution Protocol)

For each BoK suite in `docs/bok/<slug>/`, verify completeness:
```bash
for slug in $(ls docs/bok/ 2>/dev/null); do
  if [ "$slug" = "security" ]; then
    required_sec=(00-deepsearch-blueprint 01-brd-security 02-srs-secure-spec 03-sdd-hardening-architecture 04-fmea-security)
    missing=()
    for doc in "${required_sec[@]}"; do
      [ -f "docs/bok/security/$doc.md" ] || missing+=("$doc")
    done
    [ ${#missing[@]} -eq 0 ] && echo "✅ security — BoK complete (ciso-4-artifact)" || echo "⚠️ security — missing: ${missing[*]}"
    continue
  fi
  required=(00-index 01-mrd 02-brd 03-prd 04-frd 05-sdd 06-data-model 07-process-flow 08-quality-metrics)
  missing=()
  for doc in "${required[@]}"; do
    [ -f "docs/bok/$slug/$doc.md" ] || missing+=("$doc")
  done
  [ ${#missing[@]} -eq 0 ] && echo "✅ $slug — BoK complete" || echo "⚠️ $slug — missing: ${missing[*]}"
done
```

If the user mentions working on a **new module / complex feature / integration / architectural change**:
- Check whether `docs/bok/<expected-slug>/` exists with all 9 docs.
- If missing: surface in the **ALERTAS** section as a critical block per CLAUDE.md MCORCH Master Execution Protocol.
- Recommend `/bok-scribe <idea summary>` before any code is written.

## Fase 7 (opcional) — PMO handoff (`pmo-curator`)

Depois de entregar o brief, **ofereça** disparar o PMO tático: a skill `pmo-curator` lê o mesmo estado, aplica MAPE-K de PROGRESSO e materializa os próximos passos priorizados em `NEXT-STEPS.md` (un-gated vs gated, dependências, deadlines, comando exato de cada passo executável).

- **Quando oferecer:** sempre que o Sovereign, após o brief, pedir "os próximos passos / o que atacar primeiro / priorize o backlog / gere o plano".
- **Como:** invocar a skill `pmo-curator` (ou delegar ao subagente homônimo). Ela é **plan-only** — não executa nada.
- **Fronteira:** o `pmo-curator` é o loop de PROGRESSO; **não** é o guardião MAPE-K (loop de confiabilidade — infra/incidentes). SOP: `docs/processes/pmo-curator.md`.

Não force — o `/handson` continua entregando o brief como sempre; o PMO é uma camada de planejamento opcional por cima.

## Rules

- **TypeScript errors → report immediately.** If there are TS errors, list them under ALERTAS. Do not start implementing new features until errors are resolved (unless the user explicitly asks to proceed despite errors).
- **Unhealthy containers → report with triage.** Suggest the fix command if known (e.g., `docker compose restart mcorch-vector-engine` for chroma).
- **Uncommitted changes → describe, do not commit.** Only describe what exists in the working tree; committing is the user's call.
- **Keep the brief tight.** No padding. No repetition of CLAUDE.md architecture. The user already knows the architecture — they need the delta: what changed, what's broken, what's next.
- **Pending Actions priority order:** CRITICAL (before first client) > NON-CRITICAL > Phase Zeta > Core v3 > Epsilon v9.
- **Knowledge Mesh numbers:** use `GraphRAG State` section from HANDOFF.md as the source. Do not invent counts.

> 192	**One file, `engine.js`, exposing one pure function:**
> 193	
> 194	```js

> 196	```

> 198	It paints the complete frame for any time. No global mutable state, no
> 199	`requestAnimationFrame` inside it, no randomness at draw time — seed a PRNG at module
> 200	load if you need scatter. Asking for t=9.37 in isolation must give identical pixels every

> 202	
> 203	That one file drives both deliverables:
> 204	
> 205	- **HTML** — inlined into a page with a canvas, play/pause and a scrub bar.
> 206	- **MP4** — a `render.js` drives the *same file* through `@napi-rs/canvas` (`npm i

> 208	
> 209	```bash
> 210	ffmpeg -y -framerate 30 -i f_%04d.png -c:v libx264 -pix_fmt yuv420p -crf 18 \
> 211	  -preset medium -movflags +faststart out.mp4
> 212	```
> 213	
> 214	**Never fork the drawing code between preview and render.** What they scrub is what
> 215	encodes.
> 216	
> 217	**The renderer must be resumable** — skip any frame already on disk. Shell commands get
> 218	killed around 45s and a full render takes minutes; call it in 4 parallel chunks,
> 219	repeatedly, until nothing is missing. Background processes don't survive between calls.
> 220	
> 221	**Work on stills first.** Block the timeline, render 8–12 stills, tile them into a contact
> 222	sheet, *look at it*, fix, and only then render every frame:
> 223	
> 224	```bash
> 225	ffmpeg -i p_%02d.png -vf "scale=200:-1,drawtext=text='%{n}':x=6:y=6:fontsize=22:\
> 226	  fontcolor=yellow:box=1:boxcolor=black,tile=6x2" sheet.png
> 227	```
> 228	
> 229	Never render 500 frames to find out beat two is mistimed.
> 230	
> 231	Headless Chromium is usually blocked in these environments — don't try to install
> 232	Puppeteer or Playwright. Check `fc-list` for fonts before choosing one.

> 236	## 5. The craft rules — non-negotiable
> 237	
> 238	These are the whole difference between this looking expensive and looking like a template.
> 239	
> 240	1. **Bloom takes the shape of the object.** A soft oval behind something is the biggest
> 241	   tell of a cheap render. Draw 4–5 blurred, progressively larger copies of the object's
> 242	   *own silhouette*.
> 243	2. **Light breathes.** Glow amplitude swells across each beat — in, peak around two-thirds
> 244	   through, ease off before the next thing lands. Constant-intensity glow looks dead.
> 245	3. **Light comes from behind**, never as a stroke on the object. Dark objects lit from
> 246	   behind read as physical; neon outlines read as clip art.
> 247	4. **Colour moves.** No glow holds one hue for more than ~1.5s. Run it through a
> 248	   progression.
> 249	5. **Cut hard.** Where a beat ends, cut. Never soften a cut into a dissolve.
> 250	6. **Snaps snap** — 2–3 frames, not half a second. Interpolating what should be a cut is
> 251	   exactly what produces smeared, doubled, glitchy branding.
> 252	7. **Easing carries the feel.** `smoothstep` general, `easeOut` arrivals, `easeIn` exits.
> 253	   **Never** put a long move on cubic `easeIn` — nothing happens and then it lurches. That
> 254	   reads as dropped frames, and it is the number one cause of "it looks laggy".
> 255	8. **The last character typed flashes** the accent colour and cools to white over ~0.25s.
> 256	   Tiny; it's what makes typing feel live instead of pasted.
> 257	9. **Arrange, don't scatter.** Rings, grids and arcs read as designed. Random diagonal
> 258	   fly-bys read as filler.
> 259	10. **Things persist.** When one element becomes the next, keep the container and change
> 260	    only its contents. Nothing pops in from nowhere — least of all at the end.
> 261	11. **Colour helpers take *and return* hex** so they compose. A mixer returning `rgb()`
> 262	    silently breaks any `rgba()` builder downstream, and the symptom is glow that just
> 263	    doesn't render.
> 264	12. **Type sits on darkness.** If a headline lands on a bright part of the frame, put a
> 265	    soft radial scrim behind it rather than moving the type.
> 266

> 270	
> 271	- Build a contact sheet of your own stills and **look at it**. Would you ship this?
> 272	- Run a frame-difference profile — any spike that isn't a deliberate cut is a stutter:

> 275	  jerk = np.abs(np.diff(d))
> 276	  ```
> 277	- Grep the output for placeholder text and any wrong brand name.
> 278	- Confirm the encoded file's frame count and duration.

> 288	timeline or style edit, and **re-render only the affected frame range** — delete that
> 289	range from the frame cache and leave the rest. A one-beat change should take under a
> 290	minute, not a full re-render.
> 291	
> 292	Common notes and where they land:
> 293	
> 294	| they say | you change |
> 295	|---|---|
> 296	| "it lags" / "stutters" | an easing curve — almost always a long move on `easeIn` |
> 297	| "make it pop" | bloom swell amplitude, and add a colour shift |
> 298	| "too busy" | fewer objects per beat, longer holds |
> 299	| "the logo looks glitchy" | you interpolated a snap — make it 2–3 frames |
> 300	| "slower" | stretch beat durations; keep transitions the same length |
> 301	| "different vibe" | shift the palette's hue arc, keep the structure |
> 302

  "content": "// Nano Banana \u2192 C4 (Agent Plugins tree) + C10 (ChatGPT slider), sobe na Biblioteca e\n// patcheia os layers dos n\u00f3s motionScene do EP06 v3.1 (project 441a5f04).\n// Roda com: bun run scratchpad/gen-ep06-c4-c10.ts\n\nimport { createClient } from \"@supabase/supabase-js\";\n\nconst OR_KEY = process.env.OPENROUTER_API_KEY!;\nconst SB_URL = process.env.VITE_SUPABASE_URL!;\nconst SB_KEY = process.env.SB_SECRET_KEY!;\nconst USER_ID = \"ada39fae-e6cf-4dfa-a9ac-e5f31b09b569\";\nconst PROJECT = \"441a5f04-fab7-437e-8969-13cfc7c0295d\";\n\nif (!OR_KEY || !SB_URL || !SB_KEY) { console.error(\"faltam envs\"); process.exit(1); }\n\nconst sb = createClient(SB_URL, SB_KEY, { auth: { persistSession: false } });\n\nconst C4_PROMPT = `A cinematic dark panel on pure black background, Apple product reveal aesthetic crossed with synthwave. Center: a stylised dark glass code editor window showing an indented ASCII file tree in bold monospace type \u2014 top line \"agent-plugin/\", indented below \"plugin.json\", \"skills/\", \"mcp.json\". Each filename glows softly with a mint-to-cyan halo. Neon violet rim light behind the window. Below the window, a single horizontal row of six brand wordmarks written in clean white bold sans-serif, evenly spaced, 40% opacity: OpenAI, Microsoft, Amazon, Cursor, Vercel, Google. 16:9 composition, centered, symmetric, elegant, single subject, no busy background, no scattered particles.`;\n\nconst C10_PROMPT = `A cinematic dark mockup panel on pure black background, Apple product reveal aesthetic crossed with synthwave. Center: a stylised dark glass ChatGPT-like conversation window with neon cyan-violet rim light. Prominent in the middle of the panel, a large horizontal slider control: left endpoint label \"R\u00e1pido\" in white bold grotesque type, right endpoint label \"Racioc\u00ednio alto\" in white bold grotesque type, the slider knob glowing bright magenta, positioned to the right side. Small OpenAI wordmark in the top-left corner, white 60% opacity. 16:9 composition, centered, minimal, single subject, no busy background, no scattered particles.`;\n\nasync function gen(prompt: string, tag: string): Promise<Uint8Array> {\n  console.log(`[${tag}] chamando OpenRouter Nano Banana\u2026`);\n  const r = await fetch(\"https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/chat/completions\", {\n    method: \"POST\",\n    headers: {\n      Authorization: `Bearer ${OR_KEY}`,\n      \"Content-Type\": \"application/json\",\n      \"HTTP-Referer\": \"https://mcorch.com\",\n      \"X-Title\": \"MCORCH EP06 C4/C10\",\n    },\n    body: JSON.stringify({\n      model: \"google/gemini-2.5-flash-image\",\n      modalities: [\"image\", \"text\"],\n      messages: [{ role: \"user\", content: prompt }],\n    }),\n  });\n  if (!r.ok) throw new Error(`[${tag}] OR ${r.status}: ${(await r.text()).slice(0, 300)}`);\n  const data = await r.json();\n  const msg = data?.choices?.[0]?.message;\n  let b64 = \"\";\n  if (Array.isArray(msg?.content)) {\n    for (const p of msg.content) {\n      if (p?.type === \"image_url\" && p?.image_url?.url) {\n        const u = String(p.image_url.url);\n        if (u.startsWith(\"data:image/\")) b64 = u.split(\",\", 2)[1] ?? \"\";\n        break;\n      }\n    }\n  }\n  if (!b64 && Array.isArray(msg?.images) && msg.images.length > 0) {\n    const first: any = msg.images[0];\n    const u = String(typeof first === \"string\" ? first : (first?.url ?? first?.image_url?.url ?? \"\"));\n    if (u.startsWith(\"data:image/\")) b64 = u.split(\",\", 2)[1] ?? \"\";\n  }\n  if (!b64) throw new Error(`[${tag}] sem b64: ${JSON.stringify(msg).slice(0, 300)}`);\n  console.log(`[${tag}] recebeu ${b64.length} chars b64`);\n  return Uint8Array.from(Buffer.from(b64, \"base64\"));\n}\n\nasync function upload(bytes: Uint8Array, tag: string, title: string): Promise<{ id: string; key: string }> {\n  const key = `${USER_ID}/ep06-v31/${tag}-${Date.now()}.png`;\n  console.log(`[${tag}] upload \u2192 canvas-assets/${key} (${bytes.length}B)`);\n  const up = await sb.storage.from(\"canvas-assets\").upload(key, bytes, { contentType: \"image/png\", upsert: false });\n  if (up.error) throw new Error(`[${tag}] storage: ${up.error.message}`);\n  const { data: regId, error: regErr } = await sb.rpc(\"register_creative_asset\", {\n    p_user_id: USER_ID,\n    p_kind: \"image\",\n    p_storage_bucket: \"canvas-assets\",\n    p_storage_key: key,\n    p_source_module: \"spaces\",\n    p_source_job_id: `ep06-c4c10-${tag}-${Date.now()}`,\n    p_is_public: false,\n    p_mime_type: \"image/png\",\n    p_provider: \"openrouter\",\n    p_model: \"google/gemini-2.5-flash-image\",\n    p_prompt: title,\n    p_title: `EP06 v3.2 \u00b7 ${title}`,\n  });\n  if (regErr) throw new Error(`[${tag}] register: ${regErr.message}`);\n  console.log(`[${tag}] asset_id=${regId}`);\n  return { id: regId as string, key };\n}\n\nasync function patchNode(nodeId: string, assetId: string, note: string) {\n  // read-then-write com guard de updated_at (mata o autosave clobber)\n  for (let attempt = 1; attempt <= 5; attempt++) {\n    const { data: proj } = await sb.from(\"vm_canvas_projects\")\n      .select(\"graph,updated_at\").eq(\"id\", PROJECT).single();\n    const g: any = (proj as any).graph;\n    const n = g.nodes.find((x: any) => x.id === nodeId);\n    if (!n) throw new Error(`n\u00f3 ${nodeId} n\u00e3o achado`);\n    n.data = {\n      ...n.data,\n      layers: [\n        { assetId, plane: \"frente\", align: \"centro\", treatment: \"card\", scale: 1.0, mediaKind: \"image\", _note: note },\n      ],\n    };\n    const { data: up, error } = await sb.from(\"vm_canvas_projects\")\n      .update({ graph: g }).eq(\"id\", PROJECT).eq(\"updated_at\", (proj as any).updated_at).select(\"id\");\n    if (!error && up?.length) {\n      console.log(`  \u2705 patched ${nodeId} (assetId=${assetId})`);\n      return;\n    }\n    console.warn(`  \u26a0 race no attempt ${attempt}: ${error?.message ?? \"no rows\"}. retry\u2026`);\n    await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 800));\n  }\n  throw new Error(`patch ${nodeId} falhou ap\u00f3s 5 tentativas`);\n}\n\n// 1. gerar as duas em paralelo\nconst [c4bytes, c10bytes] = await Promise.all([\n  gen(C4_PROMPT, \"C4\"),\n  gen(C10_PROMPT, \"C10\"),\n]);\n\n// 2. upload sequencial (register_creative_asset serial evita corrida)\nconst c4 = await upload(c4bytes, \"c04-pasta\", \"estrutura Agent Plugins\");\nconst c10 = await upload(c10bytes, \"c10-slider\", \"slider ChatGPT racioc\u00ednio\");\n\n// 3. patchear os dois n\u00f3s\nawait patchNode(\"n_mot_c04-pasta\", c4.id, \"Nano Banana: estrutura Agent Plugins + logos\");\nawait patchNode(\"n_mot_c10-slider\", c10.id, \"Nano Banana: ChatGPT slider de racioc\u00ednio\");\n\nconsole.log(\"\\n=== RESUMO ===\");\nconsole.log(\"C4  asset_id =\", c4.id);\nconsole.log(\"C4  key      =\", c4.key);\nconsole.log(\"C10 asset_id =\", c10.id);\nconsole.log(\"C10 key      =\", c10.key);\nconsole.log(\"N\u00f3s C4/C10 do projeto\", PROJECT, \"com layers image apontando para os assets.\");\n"
}

> 1	/* Frame renderer — resumable by design.

> 3	   full render takes minutes. Every frame that already exists on disk is
> 4	   skipped, so you just call this repeatedly until nothing is missing.
> 5	
> 6	     node render.js OUTDIR                      # everything
> 7	     node render.js OUTDIR all 120 180          # a range (run 4 in parallel)
> 8	     node render.js OUTDIR preview 2.4 6.0 9.1  # stills at given seconds
> 9	     node render.js OUTDIR missing              # list gaps
> 10	*/
> 11	const { createCanvas } = require('@napi-rs/canvas');

## 🤖 Claude *(01:06:20)*

<details>
<summary>💭 Thinking Process</summary>

O contact sheet foi aprovado, mas preciso corrigir alguns problemas de timing e layout. No primeiro segundo, o texto "MESMA MESA" está em cor laranja porque a animação de `snap` ainda não avançou o suficiente, e além disso o texto ficou pequeno e desalinhado para a direita — precisa ser maior e centralizado. Estou ajustando a interpolação do tamanho para que cresça adequadamente desde o início da cena. Ah, I see the issue now — at t=1s I'm actually rendering sceneHook, not sceneLogo, since the hook scene runs from 0 to 2 seconds. So the text showing is "CINCO EMPRESAS" but it's displaying "MESMA MESA" instead, which is wrong. The preview timestamps I requested (1.0, 3.0, 5.0, 7.0) are being passed to drawFrame as global time, and it's supposed to find the correct scene by iterating through the timeline and calculating the local time offset for each scene. Ah, agora faz sentido — o rótulo "t=Xs" na verdade mostra o índice do frame no preview (0, 1, 2, 3), não o tempo real. Então estou mapeando cada frame para seu tempo correspondente: frame 0 = 1.0s real (sceneHook), frame 1 = 3.0s real (sceneLogo), frame 2 = 5.0s real (sceneUI), e frame 3 = 7.0s real (sceneGrid), e cada um está renderizando corretamente no seu respectivo ponto da timeline.

Visualmente, no frame 0 com "CINCO EMPRESAS", a última letra está piscando em verde com um bloom violeta atrás, e o typeOut está progredindo corretamente — em t=1s ele atinge cerca de 53% do texto, mostrando "CINCO E" das 14 letras totais.

No frame 1, "MESMA MESA" aparece em laranja com 90px de tamanho, centralizado no segundo tile (canto superior direito), bem alinhado.

No frame 2, há uma pill roxa com "v1.0" em branco.

No frame 3, o texto "A SEMANA FOI / DAS GRANDES" aparece em gradiente violeta para magenta em duas linhas, posicionado no quarto tile (canto inferior direito).

"CINCO EMPRESAS" ficou um pouco pequeno visualmente com 112px em canvas 1920, mas está aceitável.

Preciso verificar o shockwave em sceneLogo — ele deveria estar visível no frame 1 segundo a interpolação.

</details>

## 🤖 Claude *(02:50:51)*

<details>
<summary>💭 Thinking Process</summary>

Agora vejo como funciona: cada `.card` representa um beat da timeline, com o label sendo a palavra-chave (como "SKILL" ou "PALETA") e o body descrevendo o evento visual que acontece naquele momento — tipo a laje acendendo e o motion começando a rodar.

O Sovereign quer simplificar isso, removendo os cards textuais e deixando só ícones neon ou labels flutuantes. A solução mais rápida é desabilitar os cards do C1 inteiramente, transformando cada beat em apenas um chip pequeno com a palavra, sem o body descritivo — ou até adicionar um flag que desabilita a geração de cards quando necessário.

</details>

Encontrei o ponto crítico: os 3 cards só são renderizados quando `'nodes'` está incluído no array `elements` da especificação. Como o C1 tem `elements: ['nodes', 'runningRing', 'shockwave']`, os cards aparecem — se eu remover `'nodes'` desse array, eles desaparecem.

Tenho três caminhos: remover `'nodes'` para deixar só o motion-promo dominante e limpo; manter os cards mas convertê-los em ícones (o que exigiria modificar o motor); ou reduzir os cards a pequenos badges neon com apenas o label, removendo o corpo do texto quando o evento estiver vazio.

</details>

| Caminho | O que faço | Efeito no master |
|---|---|---|
| **A · Cortar Veo do master** (mais barato) | Deleto os 3 nós Veo do grafo (não gastou nada nos outros 2 ainda). C1/C3/C13 ficam **motion + narração ElevenLabs**. O motion-promo cereja continua entrando em C1. | 14 cenas motion + audio Sovereign. Sem presenter. Estorno em vias do P1 dá o gasto de 267 mco de qualquer forma. |

Presenter com voz IA Google (cenas Veo) + narrador voz clonada (cenas motion). Custo: 3 × +$0.02 áudio Veo (irrisório) + 534 mco dos 2 Veo faltantes. |
| **C · Veo como LAYER de motionScene** (mais cinema) | Ligo cada Veo → `motionScene.input_asset` (C1/C3/C13).
